name: Christianity vs Other Worldviews (Secularism)

objectives.text: Identify that God made everything in the world and that the world did not happen by accident
Explain in simple words that some people live as if God is not there and that the Bible calls this foolish
Recall from the catechism that people were made to glorify God and enjoy him forever
Describe what an atheist believes about God and contrast it with what the Bible teaches about God
Explain how the Bible teaches that creation shows everyone that God exists
Explain how Scripture teaches that God's law is written on every human heart so that all people know right from wrong
Compare living for present pleasures with living in light of eternity using Jesus' parable of the rich fool
Define secularism and identify secular assumptions in everyday messages such as advertising, media, and popular sayings
Explain the Christian hope of bodily resurrection and new creation as the Bible's answer to the secular claim that death is the end
Analyze the materialist claim that only matter exists by contrasting it with Scripture's teaching that God is spirit and humans have souls
Interpret how Ecclesiastes portrays life under the sun as meaningless apart from God and connect this to the modern idea of nihilism
Analyze how purely naturalistic accounts of human origins shape views of human worth and contrast them with the doctrine of the image of God
Describe how secularism developed in Western thought from the Enlightenment to the present
Analyze the postmodern claim that there is no absolute truth and compare it with Scripture's claims about truth
Analyze Paul's address at the Areopagus as a model for engaging people who do not share a biblical worldview
Analyze the moral argument that objective moral obligations require a moral lawgiver
Evaluate the core tenets of secular humanism, especially its confidence in human goodness, against Scripture's teaching on human sin
Explain how Reformed presuppositional apologetics argues that secular reasoning relies on assumptions about logic, order, and knowledge that only God supplies
Evaluate how an atheist can account for the problem of evil without a standard of good and compare this with the Reformed doctrine of providence
Defend the claim that meaning, value, and purpose require God by evaluating secular attempts to ground them
Create a written or spoken dialogue that answers a secular objection to Christianity with gentleness and respect
Synthesize an argument showing how the Christian worldview, as the Reformed tradition holds, accounts for rationality, morality, and meaning better than secularism

changes: Dropped 'people are sad without God' because it rests on feelings rather than a teachable competency, and replaced 'apply the hope we have in Jesus' with an assessable explanation of resurrection hope. Reframed the Darwinism objective as an analysis of naturalistic origins against the image of God. Merged the grade 4 'no God means no right or wrong' into a Romans 2 objective at grade 4 and a moral argument objective at grade 10. Added competencies on general revelation, identifying secular assumptions in media, the historical rise of secularism, Paul at the Areopagus, presuppositional apologetics, and crafting a gentle apologetic dialogue. Retained and reworded the remaining objectives and anchored them to specific verses and confessional articles.
